comments.why_zh: 《守望先锋》团队讲解 ECS 的好资源
comments.quote_zh: 我强烈推荐把它作为学习 ECS 的好资源
comments.text_zh: Entity 就是一组 component 实例的集合，仅此而已。ECS 中的 component 只负责数据。ECS 中的 system 只负责逻辑。如果你严格遵循这一点，那就无法支持封装或数据隐藏。OOP 并没有唯一定义，但人们普遍认为，能够进行封装（包括数据隐藏）是 OOP 的关键部分。因此，ECS 不是 OOP。证明完毕。如果你还没看过《守望先锋》团队讨论 ECS 的演讲，我强烈推荐把它作为学习 ECS 的好资源：[VIDEO] 你提到的那些语言里常用的模型可能有些与 ECS 相似，但你似乎在暗示 ECS 是 OOP 的一种形式；它不是。即使你用 Structs of Arrays、每个对象一个线程，或者你喜欢的任何方式来实现 OOP，你也不能在严格符合 ECS“component 没有逻辑”这一要求的同时，又严格符合 OOP“对象不应知道彼此的内部结构”（对象层级）这一要求。
comments.text: Entities are a collection of component instances and nothing more. Components in ECS are data-only. Systems in ECS are logic-only. If you follow this strictly, then you cannot support encapsulation or data-hiding. There is no sole definition of OOP, but it is widely accepted that the ability to do encapsulation, including data-hiding, is a key part of OOP. Therefore, ECS is not OOP. QED If you’ve not seen the Overwatch team’s talk in which they discuss ECS, I can highly recommend it as a good resource to learn about ECS: [VIDEO] There may be models commonly used in those languages you mentioned that are similar to ECS, but you seem to be implying that ECS is a form of OOP; it is not. Even if you implemented OOP using Structs of Arrays, a thread per object, or whatever you like, you cannot strictly conform with ECS’s requirement that “components have no logic” while also strictly conforming with OOP’s requirement that “objects should not know about each others’ internals” (object hierarchy).

comments.why_zh: AAA 游戏中面向数据 ECS 的最佳拆解
comments.quote_zh: 这个 Overwatch GDC 演讲是我所知道的、对 AAA 游戏中面向数据 ECS 的最佳拆解/示例
comments.text_zh: > 实体上的组件不仅定义它的数据，还通过作用于对应组件的一组系统来定义它的行为。你可以拿这些对象定义并继承它们，通过向新定义添加更多组件来增加额外行为或改变现有行为。这似乎没抓住 ECS 实际上是什么，除非你指的只是老派的实体组件做法，而不是面向数据的方式。面向数据的 ECS 做法是把状态和行为分离。实体组件本质上变成 struct，其唯一的行为可能只是一些 getter/setter 工具。行为则是无状态系统（本质上就是函数），作用于一组组件。例如，一个 PhysicsUpdateBehaviour 可能接收一个 RigidBodyComponent 和一个 HealthComponent，执行物理更新并施加基于物理/坠落的伤害。ECS 的主要好处（在我看来）甚至并不真的是性能。它通过厘清游戏循环、让实体状态如何以及何时被修改变得明显得多，使复杂游戏项目中的代码更容易管理。这类东西可能会让较小的项目变复杂，但能让更大、更复杂的项目更容易管理。这个 Overwatch GDC 演讲是我所知道的、对 AAA 游戏中面向数据 ECS 的最佳拆解/示例：[VIDEO]
comments.text: > The components on the entity define not only it's data but also it's behavior by the set of systems that act on the corresponding components. And you can take these object definitions and inherit them to add additional behavior or change the existing behavior by adding more components to the new definition. This seems to miss what ECS actually is, unless you're just referring to the old-school way of doing entity components and not the data-oriented way. Data-oriented ECS way of doing things is to separate state and behaviour. Entity components essentially become structs where their only behaviour is potentially some getter/setter utilities. Behaviours are then state-less systems (just functions, essentially) which act on a set of components. For example, a PhysicsUpdateBehaviour might take in a RigidBodyComponent and a HealthComponent to perform a physics update and apply physics/fall based damage. The main benefit of ECS (imo) isn't even really performance. It makes code in complicated game projects much easier to manage by clarifying the game loop and by making it much more obvious how and when entity state is being modified. It's the kind of thing that potentially complicates a smaller project, but makes larger more complex projects easier to manage. This Overwatch GDC talk is the best breakdown/example of data-oriented ECS in a AAA game that I know of: [VIDEO]

comments.quote_zh: 这里是 Timothy Ford 关于 Overwatch 网络代码的演讲（非常精彩）
comments.text_zh: 重要的两点是：客户端必须立刻响应用户的输入，但同时服务端必须持有权威的游戏状态。一种做法是服务端运行权威模拟，客户端把输入发给服务端，但客户端自己也跑自己的模拟。有些游戏里，客户端会尝试预测服务端会怎么做。如果客户端模拟的结果和服务端有冲突，客户端就会被回滚到服务端的状态。这通常发生在有第二个玩家以某种方式介入的时候。这里是 Timothy Ford 关于 Overwatch 网络代码的演讲（非常精彩）：[VIDEO]
comments.text: The important two points are that the client must react immediately to a user's input, but at the same time the server has to have the authoritative game state. One way of doing that is that the server runs the authoritative simulation and the clients send input to the server, but the clients also run their own simulations. In some games the client will try to predict what the server will do. If there's a conflict with what the client simulates compared to the server then the client gets rolled back to the server's state. This usually happens when there's a second player that interferes in some way. Here is a talk by Timothy Ford about Overwatch's netcode (it's really fascinating): [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 你的评论让我忍不住想提一个我最近看到的暴雪演讲，讲的是他们在《守望先锋》里使用的 ECS（Entity Component System，实体组件系统）架构。它看起来很像是“函数优先”的架构，因为他们不允许数据和函数混在一起。我不确定它有多纯粹的函数式，但它确实让我觉得是 Carmack 会欣赏的那种架构，用来处理那些复杂性——正是这些复杂性让他转向更函数式的编程风格。这个演讲是在游戏发布 3 年后做的，包含了他们从那之后获得的所有事后经验。另外，讲 netcode 的部分相当精彩，还有他们归功于使用 ECS 的预测器精度。[VIDEO]
comments.text: Your comment made me feel compelled to mention a Blizzard talk I came across recently on the ECS (Entity Component System) architecture they used for Overwatch. It looks suspiciously like a function first architecture in that they don't allow mixing of data and functions. I'm not sure how purely functional it is, but it certainly strikes me as the kind of architecture that Carmack would appreciate in dealing with complexities that lead him to a more functional programming style. This talk is 3 years after release, and includes all the hindsight they gained from that. Also, the parts talking about the netcode are quite amazing, and the precision of their predictors that they attribute to using ECS. [VIDEO]
